_meta.description: Climate risk statistics extracted from authoritative sources. Used for composite score weighting, PDF report annotations, and product copy.
_meta.extraction_method: Manual extraction from source PDFs in climate_risk_intel/

score_weights._description: Key ratios and multipliers for Phase 4 composite climate risk score weighting
score_weights.flood_loss_context: Flood is the most climate-sensitive peril with losses projected to increase by ~240% under Current Policies Scenario by 2050
score_weights.flood_concentration_context: 50% of all flood losses projected to occur in just 10% of regions
score_weights.flood_uninsured_source: ICA estimate cited in APRA Mind the Gap 2026, p.14
score_weights.flood_uninsured_context: 77% of homes facing severe to extreme flood risk are not insured for flood
score_weights.coastal_source: IPCC AR6 WGII Chapter 11, Table Box 11.6.2 (DCCEE 2011; Steffen et al. 2019)
score_weights.annual_disaster_cost_source: Deloitte 2017a, cited in IPCC AR6 WGII Chapter 11, p.38

annotations._description: Citable statistics for PDF report sections, with exact source references

flood.headline: Flood losses projected to increase 240% by 2050 under current policies
flood.detail: Flood is the most climate-sensitive weather peril. 50% of all losses concentrated in just 10% of regions. 77% of homes facing severe-to-extreme flood risk currently lack flood insurance.
flood.source: APRA Mind the Gap: Insurance Climate Vulnerability Assessment 2026

insurance_gap.headline: 1 in 7 households uninsured today, rising to 1 in 4 by 2050
insurance_gap.detail: Around 15% of Australian households (1.4 million) currently face high insurance affordability pressure. By 2050, ~25% may be without home insurance — an additional 1 million households. Equivalent to ~40,000 households losing coverage per year.
insurance_gap.source: APRA Mind the Gap: Insurance Climate Vulnerability Assessment 2026

premium_growth.headline: Home insurance premiums rising 7.2% annually vs wages at 3.1%
premium_growth.detail: Between 2010 and 2025, Australian home insurance premiums rose by an annual average of 7.2%, while wages grew by 3.1%. Taxes and levies add ~21% nationally (higher in NSW due to ESL at ~18%).
premium_growth.source: APRA Mind the Gap: Insurance Climate Vulnerability Assessment 2026

weather_losses.headline: National weather losses: $7B today → $16B by 2050
weather_losses.detail: Expected national weather losses increasing from less than $7 billion annually in 2024 to over $16 billion annually in 2050 under the Current Policies Scenario.
weather_losses.source: APRA Mind the Gap: Insurance Climate Vulnerability Assessment 2026

coastal.headline: $164-226 billion in coastal infrastructure exposed to 1.1m sea level rise
coastal.detail: With 1.1m SLR: 187,000-274,000 residential buildings, 5,800-8,600 commercial buildings, 27,000-35,000km roads and 1,200-1,500km rail exposed. 111% rise in inundation cost from 2020 to 2100.
coastal.source: IPCC AR6 WGII Chapter 11, Table Box 11.6.2

bushfire.headline: 2019-20 bushfires: $8B+ cost, 5.8-8.1M hectares burned
bushfire.detail: 33 direct deaths, 429 smoke-related deaths, $2.3B insured losses, $3.6B tourism/agriculture losses, $1.95B health costs. Climate impacts are cascading and compounding (high confidence).
bushfire.source: IPCC AR6 WGII Chapter 11; ICA Catastrophe Resilience 2024-25

catastrophe_season_2024_25.headline: $1.97B insured losses from declared extreme weather events in 2024-25
catastrophe_season_2024_25.detail: 154,100 claims, $13K average claim. 25% decrease from prior year ($2.61B). Five-year total ~$22.5B insured extreme weather costs, a 67% jump from the previous five-year period.

flood_properties_at_risk.headline: 1.36 million properties at flood risk, 298,000 at severe-to-extreme risk
flood_properties_at_risk.detail: 242,000 residential dwellings with highest flood risk. ICA estimates 186,000 of these not insured for flood. Rebuilding just 10% would cost >$9 billion.

heat.headline: Days over 35°C projected to increase 80-350% by 2090
heat.detail: Unprecedented extreme temperatures as high as 50°C in Sydney possible with 2.0°C global warming. Heat-related deaths in Sydney/Melbourne/Brisbane: 142/year (1971-2020) → 300-600/year (2031-2080).

compound_risk.headline: Climate impacts are cascading and compounding across systems (high confidence)
compound_risk.detail: Complex connections generating new types of risks, exacerbating existing stressors and constraining adaptation options. Multi-hazard interaction (flood + heat + fire + drought) creates compounding recovery costs.
compound_risk.source: IPCC AR6 WGII Fact Sheet Australasia
